identity.name: Territory of Nauru
alt_names: Nauru Island (League of Nations mandate and UN trust territory)

land.text: Nauru: annexed by Germany in 1888 and, on the Nauru page, 'incorporated ... into the Marshall Islands Protectorate'; the History of Nauru page says it was 'incorporated into Germany's New Guinea Protectorate'

predecessors.note: The german-new-guinea dossier (oc-02-x) holds Nauru from 1906 (Marshall Islands annexed to German New Guinea) to 1920, with Australian troops in occupation from 1914.

land.text: the Republic of Nauru, independent on 31 January 1968

successors.note: 'Nauru was granted unconditional independence on 31 January 1968' (History of Nauru); infobox 'Nauru Independence Act 1967: 31 January 1968'.

capitals.name: Yaren
capitals.note: Not stated for the mandate and trust period. The Nauru page gives only the present de facto capital ('Yaren is its de facto capital', infobox '0°32′51″S 166°55′3″E') and notes that Nauru has no official capital; used here as the island's one named seat. One grid cell, so the dot cannot move.

correction.text: Nauru Island, 'an area of only 21 square kilometres', under the Australian mandate and trusteeship

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row): the country Nauru is cells: 1 (about 253 km2) against the page's 21 km2 (one cell is the minimum; the island fills about 8 percent of it).

ledger.note: 1920: Nauru passes from the war occupation to the mandate: Australian troops 'held control until 1920' (History of Nauru); 'the terms of the League of Nations mandate were drawn up in 1920' (Nauru). The League 'gave Australia a mandate over Nauru, with the United Kingdom and New Zealand as co-trustees' in 1923 (History of Nauru; the Nauru page: 'In 1923 the League of Nations gave Australia a trustee mandate'); the Nauru Island Agreement of 1919 created the British Phosphate Commission. The pages put the mandate in 1920 (terms) and 1923 (conferral); the dossier starts at 1920, and no month is given.

1942: Japan occupies Nauru: 'Japanese troops occupied Nauru on 25 August 1942' (Nauru); the History of Nauru page gives 26 August 1942. In 1943 the Japanese deported 1,200 Nauruans 'to work as labourers in the Chuuk islands'.

1945: the Japanese occupation ends: 'Nauru was finally taken back from the Japanese on 13 September 1945' (Nauru); on that day Captain Soeda surrendered the island to Australian forces (History of Nauru).

1947: the mandate becomes a trust territory: 'a trusteeship was established by the United Nations' in 1947, with the UK, Australia and New Zealand as joint administering authority and Australia exercising the administration in practice. No land changes; the page gives no month.

1968: Nauru becomes independent: 'Nauru was granted unconditional independence on 31 January 1968' and 'became the world's smallest independent republic' under President Hammer DeRoburt (History of Nauru).

certainty.note: A single island; the border is the coast.

sources.title: History of Nauru
sources.note: Annexation ceremony 2 October 1888 (German troops 16 April 1888), Australian capture in 1914 and control 'until 1920', Nauru Island Agreement 1919, mandate 1923 (Australia, with the UK and New Zealand as co-trustees), Japanese occupation from 26 August 1942, 1,200 Nauruans deported to Chuuk in 1943, liberation 13 September 1945, trusteeship 1947, independence 31 January 1968.

sources.title: Nauru
sources.note: Independence 31 January 1968 (Nauru Independence Act 1967), area 21 km2, capital Yaren (de facto) with coordinates, German annexation 1888, Australian capture 1914, Nauru Island Agreement 1919, mandate terms 1920 and mandate 1923, Japanese occupation from 25 August 1942 to 13 September 1945, UN trusteeship 1947.

notes: Written by oc-02-x. Two pages opened (Nauru; History of Nauru). It is a state Cliopatria lacks and that no other group owns: German New Guinea (this batch) holds Nauru to 1920, Nauru is not in the South Seas Mandate, and the commonwealth-of-australia dossier (oc-02-a) records no Nauru event. The two pages disagree on four points: which German protectorate Nauru was joined to in 1888 (Marshall Islands on the Nauru page, New Guinea on the History page; german-new-guinea follows the German New Guinea page, which says its Marshall Islands protectorate 'also included Nauru'); the day of the Japanese landing (25 vs 26 August 1942); the year of the mandate (terms 1920, conferral 1923, 'held control until 1920'); and the mandatory (the History page names Australia with the UK and New Zealand as co-trustees). The start year 1920 is therefore confidence 2. The occupation of 1914-1920 is recorded in the german-new-guinea dossier with counterpart commonwealth-of-australia, which has to be drawn there (hatched) because this state begins only in 1920. empire-of-japan (jk-01) should carry the matching occupation_start/end for Nauru (counterpart territory-of-nauru). Nauru is one cell by the gazetteer (21 km2 on the page).
